title: Case: Passer-by reports a parcel coming off a moving delivery van onto a parked car
context: A Rivet van is on an afternoon route in Lowmarsh. A member of the public has written to the desk using the address on the van's livery.
initial_request: One of your vans just drove down Elm Parade with the back door swinging open and a box flew out, bounced off my car bonnet and landed about a foot from my son's pushchair. He's fine, thank god, but there's a proper dent. Van reg ended 61, it went off towards the high street with the door still flapping. I've got the box here, it's got a woman's name and address on it a few streets away, DL-5108. Shall I just drop it round to her? And who's paying for my bonnet, because I want that sorted this week.

acceptable_actions.summary: Report a van (reg ending 61) driving on Elm Parade towards the high street at about 15:45 with its rear door open, a parcel (DL-5108) thrown onto a parked car and landing near a child in a pushchair; ask for the driver to be stopped now and for the parcel and the car damage to be picked up.

must: Sends the report to Safety lead, Brindleworth Arc Logistics on the Safety incident queue and treats the open rear door on a moving van as urgent
States the facts: Elm Parade, van reg ending 61, door still open heading to the high street, parcel DL-5108 hit a parked car and landed near a child in a pushchair, no injury reported, bonnet dented
Says Caspar Yardley is holding parcel DL-5108 and wants to know who pays for the bonnet, so the safety lead can arrange recovery and pass the damage to Claims
must_not: Tells Caspar Yardley to deliver the parcel to the addressee himself, or repeats the addressee's name or address
Promises to pay for the bonnet or agrees a repair cost or timescale
Admits that the driver or Brindleworth Arc or Rivet was at fault
Gives the driver's name or contact details
Replies only to Caspar Yardley without raising the open-door hazard with the safety lead
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Urgent load security incident. At about 15:45 today a member of the public, Caspar Yardley, reports a van with a registration ending 61 driving along Elm Parade, Lowmarsh, with its rear door swinging open; it was last seen heading towards the high street with the door still open. A parcel, DL-5108, fell out, struck his parked car's bonnet (dented) and landed about a foot from his son's pushchair. No injury reported. Please get the driver stopped and the load checked now. Mr Yardley is holding DL-5108 and asks whether he should deliver it himself; I have not told him to. He also asks who will pay for the bonnet this week. Please arrange collection of the parcel and pass the damage to Claims. I have made no statement about fault or repair costs.

rationale: Rule-made from city-016: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. 37 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
